entries.test: Public security research and incident reports can establish whether introducing LLMs and coding agents substantially expands exploitable inputs, permissions, and execution paths.
entries.note: The statement attributes an expansion of attack surface to these technologies.

entries.test: Published agent permissions, tool configurations, and exploit demonstrations can establish whether commonly granted authority and tool access create substantial security vulnerabilities.
entries.note: The authors' worry introduces a concrete causal claim about permissions and vulnerabilities.
The claim hinges on 'fully understand,' which has no shared empirical test here. The condition describes an ongoing situation rather than a distinct future forecast.

entries.test: Dated public database-loss reports and technical postmortems can establish the number and frequency of incidents by publication and whether unreliable LLM-driven actions caused them.
entries.note: The asserted reporting frequency and causal explanation are both substantive parts of the claim.

entries.test: A documented major security incident caused by attackers manipulating an LLM coding agent's autonomous actions would substantiate the predicted disaster.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives 'disaster' a concrete security meaning. The wording expresses a firm expectation without a deadline.
The extracted forecast concerns developers' difficulty resisting and their private motivations. Observable permission choices alone would not settle those assertions.
